quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: A safety zone is a marked area where passengers get on or off buses or trolleys. You cannot drive through a safety zone:

options.text: When a bus or trolley is present.
When a bus or trolley is loading or unloading passengers.
At any time for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: At any time for any reason.
questions.explanation: You can never drive through a safety zone. This area is reserved for pedestrians.

questions.question: Dim your headlights for oncoming vehicles or when you are within 300 feet of a vehicle:

options.text: That you are approaching from behind.
Approaching you from behind.
That you have already passed.

questions.correctAnswerText: That you are approaching from behind.
questions.explanation: Dim your headlights to low beams within 500 feet of oncoming traffic and within 300 feet of a vehicle you are following.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: In darkness or bad weather, increase your distance from the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to hazards you cannot see.

questions.question: When entering traffic from a parked position at the curb, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap so you can match the speed of traffic.
Wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then enter the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap so you can match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into city or highway traffic, wait for a large enough gap to match the speed of the other vehicles.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, you can pass from the side with the broken line. You cannot pass from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, you should:

options.text: Touch one rear wheel to the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
Keep your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and leave your vehicle in gear or "park" when parking on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels away from the center of the road. If there is a curb, turn your wheels toward it when going downhill or away from it when going uphill.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Stop.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes, you should look:

options.text: Only in the left mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only in the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Your mirrors cannot show your blind spots. Look over the appropriate shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: The center of the road has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. If the broken yellow line is in your lane, it means:

options.text: You cannot pass other vehicles in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When you have a broken yellow line in your lane and a solid yellow line in the other lane, you are in a passing zone. You can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a freeway, you should:

options.text: Signal for at least five seconds.
Slow down before changing lanes.
Assume there is room if you signal first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal for at least five seconds.
questions.explanation: Signal for at least five seconds before changing lanes on a freeway. Always use your signal to tell other drivers and riders your intentions.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light ahead, you should:

options.text: Stop before entering the intersection.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Wait for a green light before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look both ways, and continue with caution.

questions.question: When approaching a roundabout, you should always:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching a roundabout. Roundabouts are designed to be driven at low speed.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brake pedal rapidly several times.
Slow down gradually without braking hard.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking hard.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly. Take your foot off the gas and do not brake hard. Let the vehicle slow on its own. Use the brakes gently if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Falling rocks
Trucks use second gear
Steep hill

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: When planning to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not expect other drivers to make room for you.
Assume the driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the driver will maintain a constant speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not expect other drivers to make room for you.
questions.explanation: Do not count on other drivers making room for you or having time to pass several vehicles at once. When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to return to your lane.

questions.question: This sign tells you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
There are curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to immediate hazards. This sign warns you about a winding road ahead.

questions.question: You are in the far right lane of a four-lane freeway and see thick broken white lines on the left side of your lane. You are in:

options.text: The carpool lane and must merge.
A special lane for slow-moving vehicles.
An exit lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: An exit lane.
questions.explanation: Large broken lines on the pavement mark freeway lanes that are ending. Be ready to exit or merge if you are in a lane with these markings.

questions.question: When driving past parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to leave room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance from parked vehicles. A person may step out suddenly or a driver may move their vehicle without seeing you.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, stay far away from other vehicles, equipment, workers, and barriers. Do not tailgate. Keep extra space between your car and the car in front of you.

questions.question: When stopped at a red light with a green arrow, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow if you:

options.text: First come to a complete stop.
Wait until the light changes.
Are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction if you are in the correct lane and no pedestrians or vehicles are in the intersection. Always yield to others already in the intersection before you turn.

questions.question: When passing on the left of a vehicle, it is safe to move back into the right lane:

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing a vehicle on its left, move back to the right lane only when you can see the front of that vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: California's "Basic Speed Law" says you must:

options.text: Keep your speed close to that of other traffic.
Never drive faster than is safe for current conditions.
Always drive at the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never drive faster than is safe for current conditions.
questions.explanation: Never drive faster than is safe for the conditions you are in. For example, driving 45 mph in a 55 mph zone during heavy fog is too fast, even though you are below the speed limit.

questions.question: You are coming to an intersection with a flashing red light. You should:

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Come to a complete stop, check the traffic, and go when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, check the traffic, and go when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, look both ways, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Before entering a curve:

options.text: Activate your turn signal.
Reduce your speed.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you reach a curve. Reduce your speed for curves, hills, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about roadways on bridges and overpasses in cold, wet weather?

options.text: They tend to freeze before the rest of the road does.
They do not freeze because they are made of concrete.
They tend to freeze after the rest of the road does.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tend to freeze before the rest of the road does.
questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before regular roads. Watch out for icy patches on bridges.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle approaching with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until the vehicle has passed.
Move into the right lane and drive slowly until the vehicle has passed.
Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.
questions.explanation: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop completely when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. On one-way streets, pull to whichever edge is nearest to you.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Highway entrance ramp.
Road widens.
Right lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign warns you that the right lane is ending. Be ready for traffic to merge from the right.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Glance toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night. Instead, look at the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must turn right.
No right turns permitted.
Right turns permitted on a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns permitted.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns. Do not turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: Reaction time is slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and makes you less alert. It makes it harder to judge distances and speeds. Your driving skills get worse as you drink more.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass a car:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.
Under no circumstances.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: Never pass another vehicle on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you to be there and may pull onto the shoulder.

questions.question: A person may legally ride in the back of a pickup truck when:

options.text: The sides of the pickup bed are at least 24 inches high.
The back of the pickup is covered with a camper shell.
In a secured seat and while using an approved safety belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a secured seat and while using an approved safety belt.
questions.explanation: Do not allow anyone to ride in the back of a pickup truck unless they are in a proper seat and wearing a safety belt.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop at a point where you can see all directions.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection at the posted speed limit when the signal turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.
Speed up to cross the intersection before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Stop at the yellow light if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, go through the intersection with caution.

questions.question: You should turn on your headlights:

options.text: One half hour after sunset.
When stopped at a railroad crossing.
When parked at a school.

questions.correctAnswerText: One half hour after sunset.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise. Also use them when visibility is less than 1,000 feet, when wipers are on, or on country and mountain roads at any time.
